title: Rulezet YARA rule template
description: Every piece of a YARA rule that Rulezet reads when a rule is created or imported: the rule header and each key of the meta: section, the Rulezet field it fills, and how to write it. Companion guide: yara_template.md.

general_syntax.meta_entry: key = "value"  (identifier, '=', double-quoted string; integers and true/false are valid YARA but only reach the extra metadata, never title/author/version/license/uuid)
general_syntax.first_meta_block_only: author, description, license, version, id/uuid and source are read from the FIRST meta: block of the file — one rule per file gives predictable results.
general_syntax.repeated_keys: A key may be repeated (reference = "…" twice): every value is kept in references/extra metadata, but for the main fields (description, author…) the last value wins.
general_syntax.lists: A list is one string, items separated by commas: "a, b, c". Tags also accept spaces, ';' and '|'.
general_syntax.comments: Keys inside // or /* */ comments are ignored by tag and metadata extraction.
general_syntax.escaping: Escape a double quote as \" and a backslash as \\ inside a value.

rule_name.how_to_write: rule Name_Of_The_Rule { … } — letters, digits and '_', not starting with a digit, max 128 characters. The rule name IS the title on Rulezet (there is no title meta key).

rule_tags.how_to_write: rule Name : tag1 tag2 tag3 — identifiers separated by spaces after a colon. Lower-cased on Rulezet ('Ransomware' and 'ransomware' are one tag).

modifiers.how_to_write: Avoid 'global rule': its condition is ANDed into every other rule of the namespace — Rulezet flags it as a risk. 'private rule' is fine for helper rules.

imports.how_to_write: import "pe" / "math" / "hash"… on top of the file, before the rule.

dependencies.how_to_write: Naming another rule in the condition makes it a dependency: Rulezet resolves it from rules already on the instance (validation fails if it can't).

description.how_to_write: One or two sentences: what it detects and why. Vulnerability ids written here (CVE-2024-1234, GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, GCVE-…) are linked to the rule as vulnerabilities — this is the ONLY place Rulezet reads them from for YARA.
description.example: Detects the Example loader dropped by exploitation of CVE-2024-1234

author.how_to_write: Name, handle or team. Several authors: "Alice, Bob".
author.default_if_missing: author of the import (GitHub repo owner) or Unknown

modified.how_to_write: ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD, date of the last change.

version.how_to_write: Quoted: "1.0", "1.2". An unquoted number is ignored (version falls back to 1.0).

license.how_to_write: An SPDX identifier, or the license name / URL.
license.default_if_missing: license of the imported repo, or unknown

id.how_to_write: A UUID v4, generated once and NEVER changed: it is how Rulezet recognises the same rule on re-import (duplicate check, GitHub updates, connectors). 'id' is read before 'uuid'.

reference.how_to_write: One URL per entry; repeat the key for several (reference = "…" on two lines). Up to 50 kept. A MITRE URL (attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001) also maps the technique.
reference.counts_for: documentation score (has_reference — only 'reference' and 'reference_url' count there)

source.how_to_write: Where the rule comes from (project, repo URL). On a GitHub import the repo URL wins.
source.default_if_missing: repo URL of the import, or Unknown

tags.how_to_write: "tag1, tag2, tag3" — separators , ; | or spaces. 'namespace:value' is one tag ("exploit: cve-2024-1234" → exploit:cve-2024-1234). Platform words (windows, linux, macos, aws…) also set the rule's platform badges. Not shown in the extra metadata.

tlp.how_to_write: "TLP:AMBER", "tlp:amber" or just "AMBER". Must match a tlp:* tag of the instance.

mitre_attack.how_to_write: Technique ids, comma separated: "T1059.001, T1105". Sub-techniques as T1234.001.

hash.rulezet_field: extra metadata (hash type MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 detected and shown)
hash.how_to_write: One sample hash per entry, repeat the key for several. Hex only.

filetype.how_to_write: PE, ELF, Mach-O, PDF, Office, Script…

severity.how_to_write: One of the values, lower case.

confidence.how_to_write: One of the values, lower case.

status.how_to_write: One of the values, lower case.

falsepositives.how_to_write: Known benign matches, or "None known". false_positives / known_false_positives are kept as long text.
falsepositives.example: Packed installers using the same stub

any_other_key.rulezet_field: extra metadata (shown as-is on the rule page)
any_other_key.how_to_write: Any other identifier = value is kept and displayed (max 40 keys, 20 values per key, 300 characters per value).

example_rule:
import "pe"

rule MAL_Example_Loader_Nov26 : loader windows
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects the Example loader dropped by exploitation of CVE-2024-1234"
        author = "Jane Doe (@janedoe)"
        date = "2026-11-23"
        modified = "2026-11-23"
        version = "1.0"
        license = "DRL-1.1"
        id = "5d1c9a6e-3b2f-4c8e-9a1d-7f4e2b6c8a10"
        reference = "https://example.org/blog/example-loader-analysis"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/"
        source = "https://github.com/example-org/yara-rules"
        tags = "ransomware, exploit:cve-2024-1234"
        tlp = "TLP:CLEAR"
        pap = "PAP:CLEAR"
        mitre_attack = "T1059.001, T1105"
        hash = "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
        malware_family = "ExampleLoader"
        threat_actor = "APT-Example"
        malware_type = "Loader"
        os = "Windows"
        filetype = "PE"
        severity = "high"
        score = 75
        confidence = "medium"
        status = "experimental"
        falsepositives = "Packed installers using the same stub"

    strings:
        $s1 = "ExampleLoader/1.0" ascii wide
        $s2 = { 4D 5A 90 00 03 00 00 00 }
        $s3 = "cmd.exe /c powershell -enc" ascii nocase

    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and filesize < 2MB and pe.number_of_sections > 2 and 2 of ($s*)
}
